QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_43

question.text: The collateral that a clearing member deposits as liquid assets must satisfy which composition requirement?

answer.text: Total liquid assets must comprise at least 50% cash component, with the cash component including cash, bank guarantees, fixed deposit receipts, T-bills and dated government securities
At least 75% must be in dated government securities
No composition requirement exists; any form of collateral is acceptable

explanation.text: The Logic: Collateral deposits are divided into cash and non-cash components. The cash component is defined to include cash, bank guarantees, fixed deposit receipts, T-bills and dated government securities. The source requires that total liquid assets comprise at least 50% cash component, with the balance permitted in approved non-cash collateral. The Trap: The 50% floor applies to the cash component as defined by the source - not strictly to physical cash. Non-cash collateral cannot make up more than 50% of total liquid assets. Note: Source: NISM-Series-VIII workbook (Dec 2025), pages 178 and 180.
